common_name: Playin' the Blues Salvia (Blue-Violet Autumn Sage Hybrid)
scientific_name: Salvia greggii x microphylla 'Playin' the Blues'

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Playin' the Blues is valued for true blue-violet flowers, an unusually cool color for this typically red- and pink-flowered hybrid group.

directions: Plant in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun, and avoid overwatering, since this Texas-native-derived subshrub is prone to root rot in soggy or heavy clay soil. Playin' the Blues stands out from most autumn sage hybrids for its true blue-violet flowers, opening in continuous flushes from spring through hard frost and drawing hummingbirds and bees steadily throughout the growing season. Its compact, well-branched habit suits mixed borders, xeriscape plantings, and pollinator gardens, and a hard cutback in late winter keeps the plant dense and encourages the heaviest bloom. Extremely drought-tolerant once established, it thrives on lean soil with minimal supplemental water.

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or nursery starts after frost danger passes in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; this UK-raised baby sage selection carries warm coral-salmon flowers over compact, well-branched growth.

directions: Give Christine Yeo full sun and well-drained, moderately fertile soil; it forms a tidy, rounded mound of aromatic foliage covered in warm coral-salmon flowers from late spring through hard frost, pausing only briefly at the height of summer heat. It is a reliable hummingbird and bee plant for a mixed border or pollinator bed, and its color is a useful bridge between the hot reds and pinks common in this hybrid group and true orange tones. Shear lightly after each flush to keep growth dense and encourage rebloom, and take cuttings in fall as insurance since plants can decline in cold, wet winter soil.

common_name: Icing Sugar Salvia (Pink and White Bicolor Baby Sage)

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or nursery starts after frost danger passes in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Icing Sugar is grown for its distinctive bicolor flowers combining bright pink upper lips with white lower lips.

directions: Give Icing Sugar full sun and well-drained, moderately fertile soil; this popular baby sage selection produces eye-catching bicolor flowers, with bright pink upper lips contrasting against white lower lips, on a compact, well-branched mound of aromatic foliage from late spring through hard frost. It is an outstanding hummingbird and bee plant for a mixed border, cottage garden, or container. Shear lightly after each flush to maintain dense growth and encourage continued rebloom, and take cuttings in fall as insurance since plants can be short-lived in cold, wet winter soil.

common_name: Sensation Deep Rose Salvia (Compact Deep Rose-Pink Meadow Sage)

planting.note: Plant container plants or seed-grown transplants in spring in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; Sensation Deep Rose is a compact, early-flowering seed strain within the Sensation series, prized for its deep rose-pink flower spikes on a dwarf, uniform habit.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun. Sensation Deep Rose is a dwarf, seed-grown selection of hardy meadow sage bred for a compact, uniform habit and dense spikes of deep rose-pink flowers, making it well suited to bedding displays, edging, and the front of a sunny border where taller nemorosa cultivars would be out of scale. Shearing the plant back by about half after the first flush of bloom encourages a strong second round of flowers into late summer. It is drought-tolerant once established, rarely bothered by deer or rabbits, and draws bees throughout its bloom season; in hot, humid zone 9 summers it may decline and is best treated as a shorter-lived perennial refreshed every few years.
